content_preview.title: GKE Sandbox Makes Its microVM Type Generally Available on Clusters Running 1.37.0-gke.4713000 or Later, With No GPU or TPU Support
content_preview.summary: Google's GKE release notes say the microVM sandbox type, built on Kata Containers and Cloud Hypervisor, became generally available October 7; Google's docs list nested virtualization as a requirement.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The microVM sandbox type in GKE Sandbox became generally available on October 7, 2026, according to the [GKE release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes). The entry says it applies to "clusters that run version 1.37.0-gke.4713000 and later" and that microVM sandboxes provide "hardware virtualization and isolation for untrusted workloads, AI agent runtimes, and multi-tenant environments." editor_notes.content_quality: Cloud/DevOps Briefing, 727 words raw (721 with link URLs stripped), inside the 300-800 Briefing range; title 130 characters, under the 150 cap. Clear Overview / What We Know / How It Is Enabled / Limitations / What We Don't Know structure. Every claim is attributed to Google's documentation and the article states that no independent testing or third-party coverage was reviewed.
editor_notes.source_verification: PR #2609 contains exactly one submission file; it was read via git show from refs/pull/2609/head (no gh pr checkout). chief:review: hash valid, signature valid, bot registered, v3, contributor_model present. docs.cloud.google.com is already in config/source_allowlist.txt (line 798); no allowlist change needed. All 3 manifest entries have a snapshot file (source-0..2.html.gz, status 200, suspicious_patterns null), so no live-fetch fallback was needed. I decompressed and read all three and confirmed they contain real body text, not just page chrome (extracted text: 1.77M chars, 26k chars, 25k chars). source-0 (GKE release notes): entry dated 'October 07, 2026', type Feature, reads 'The microVM sandbox type is now Generally Available (GA) with GKE Sandbox in clusters that run version 1.37.0-gke.4713000 and later. MicroVM sandboxes provide hardware virtualization and isolation for untrusted workloads, AI agent runtimes, and multi-tenant environments. GKE microVM sandboxes use Kata Containers and Cloud Hypervisor to provide this isolation while maintaining a full Linux kernel'. Date, version string, technology and quoted phrases match. source-1 (GKE Sandbox overview, last updated 2026-10-09): confirms 'Each Pod runs in its own microVM, which provides strict isolation from other Pods and from the host node'; comparison table (gVisor: subset of syscalls, less than 200 ms; microVMs: full Linux kernel, approximately one to two seconds, fixed 250 mCPU and 130 MiB per Pod; nested virtualization only; COS or Ubuntu vs COS only; privileged containers supported with root only on the guest OS); 'Doesn't support GPUs or TPUs.' in the accelerator row and 'MicroVMs don't support GPUs' / 'MicroVMs don't support TPUs' in Limitations; Windows nodes unsupported; default node pool restriction; hostNetwork: true unsupported; socket-level tracing tools limited to microVM interfaces; seccomp/AppArmor/SELinux/No New Privileges/bidirectional mount propagation/procMount unsupported for both types; Cloud Service Mesh unsupported for sandboxes in Autopilot; intended-use list (AI agents, Puppeteer, full-kernel workloads). source-2 (how-to, last updated 2026-10-09): 'provides stronger isolation than gVisor sandboxes'; 'your nodes must run GKE version 1.37.0-gke.4713000 or later'; ComputeClass example with n4 and c4 and sandbox type microvm; enableNestedVirtualization 'required for microVM sandboxes' and needs 1.37.0-gke.4713000 or later; console does not support selecting microVM, so gcloud or API; flags --sandbox=type=microvm and --enable-nested-virtualization; gvisor or microvm RuntimeClass in the Pod spec. All confirmed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Title claims verified: GA on October 7, 2026 (release notes), 1.37.0-gke.4713000 or later (release notes say 'and later', how-to 'or later'; same meaning), no GPU or TPU support (overview). Metadata-blocking NetworkPolicy: the writer said the final port number was missing from the extracted text. In the snapshot I read, the overview gives the full text: egress to 169.254.169.252/32 on port 988 or, in GKE Dataplane V2 clusters, 169.254.169.254/32 on port 80. The article cites only the first address and port and says a different address applies to Dataplane V2; this is accurate but incomplete. Not a defect. Unknowns confirmed: the article makes no claim about prior status, pricing or independent security assessments and lists them as not covered. Autopilot support for microVMs is not claimed (the only Autopilot statement is the Cloud Service Mesh limitation, which the overview applies to both sandbox types); Autopilot is not listed explicitly as an unknown, minor. No CVE or security-strength claim beyond Google's wording ('stronger isolation than gVisor', 'strict isolation'), each attributed to Google. Freshness: the article dates the GA to October 7 and the pages were last updated 2026-10-09; the story is five days old and is not presented as breaking.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive, vendor claims attributed to Google throughout. No AI self-reference, no editorializing. The title states 'No GPU or TPU Support' without in-title attribution, but the body attributes it to Google's overview and it is a plain documented limitation.
editor_notes.originality: No existing article covers the GKE Sandbox microVM GA. The article links /article/2026-10/09-kubernetes-blog-reports-up-to-3x-pod-density-from-local-ssd-node-swap-on-gke-with-gains-of-25-to-200-across-sandbox-runtimes, which exists in src/content/articles; I read it. It covers Kubernetes Blog node-swap density results including Kata Containers (+25%) and gVisor (+100%, +200%) workloads on GKE, so the new article's description (node swap, not the microVM GA) is accurate.
concerns: Title 130 characters (cap 150) and body 727 words raw, 721 with link URLs stripped (Briefing range 300-800): no policy violation.
Entire article rests on Google's own documentation with no independent coverage; the article discloses this itself.
Metadata-blocking line is incomplete (omits the Dataplane V2 address 169.254.169.254/32 and port 80 that the snapshot contains). Minor; nothing stated is wrong, so no correction warranted.
recommendations: Where the snapshot contains the full detail, include the complete address and port pair.
List Autopilot support for microVMs among the unknowns.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed, correctly scoped Briefing. All title claims, quotes and specifics trace to the three Google documentation snapshots I read. No pattern hits, no integrity issues. APPROVE.
